title: Bentong Monsoon Marathon 2026 Review: Racing Through a Rainforest Retreat
seo_title: Bentong Monsoon Marathon 2026 Review | Janda Baik
meta_description: Bentong Monsoon Marathon 2026 review: November 28 at Janda Baik -- a rainforest village near Kuala Lumpur, honestly named for wet-season racing.
dek: Set for 28 November 2026 at Janda Baik, a rainforest retreat village 45km from Kuala Lumpur, this marathon's name is an honest heads-up about running through Malaysia's wet season.
verdict: The Bentong Monsoon Marathon takes its name seriously -- it's held at Janda Baik, a rainforest village 800m above sea level in Bentong District, Pahang, during Malaysia's wetter months, and the race name itself is a direct acknowledgement of likely rain rather than a marketing euphemism. Janda Baik carries genuine local character: its name means 'good widow' or 'the divorcee returns,' first settled in 1930 by villagers displaced from a 1926 flood. Two serious distances (42K/21K) and no shorter fun-run category make this squarely for committed distance runners prepared for wet-weather trail-adjacent conditions.

sections.heading: A Name That Doesn't Hide the Weather
paragraphs: The Bentong Monsoon Marathon offers two distances: the 42.195K full marathon and 21.1K half marathon, at Janda Baik, Bentong, Pahang. [1] Unlike most races that avoid mentioning weather risk in their branding, this one names it directly -- a genuinely honest signal about what to expect running in Malaysia during its wetter season.

sections.heading: Janda Baik: A Rainforest Retreat Near KL
paragraphs: Janda Baik is a village in Bentong District, Pahang, about 45km from Kuala Lumpur and 800m above sea level. [2] The name means 'the divorcee returns' or 'good widow' in Malay -- first settled in 1930 by three Bentong villagers who relocated after their town flooded in 1926. Today it's known for its rainforests, intimate resorts, and small farm holdings, with activities like biking, tubing, ATV trail-blazing and rafting available for visitors.

sections.heading: A Village Balancing Tourism and Environment
paragraphs: While Janda Baik historically focused on agriculture, it now also embraces electronics and tourism industries -- though that development has led to deforestation concerns and protests from villagers worried about ecosystem and cultural impacts. [2] Running a race through this kind of actively-debated development landscape gives the course genuine, if complicated, local relevance.

sections.heading: Serious Distances, No Fun Run
paragraphs: Only the full marathon and half marathon are offered -- no shorter category -- similar to the Selangor Marathon's focused format covered elsewhere in this research batch. [1] Registration is currently open.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a scenic marathon through a rainforest retreat village near Kuala Lumpur appeals -- and you're genuinely prepared for wet conditions given the race's own honest naming -- the Bentong Monsoon Marathon on 28 November 2026 is a distinctive, committed-runner-focused pick. Pack for rain regardless of forecast.
